body_markdown:
Yes, there is an AI agent that can apply to jobs on Workday and other ATS portals.[Tsenta](https://tsenta.com/) applies to jobs on Workday and 30+ other employer systems (ATSes), including Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and iCIMS. It handles the employer's account and verification steps where supported, fills every page of the form from your saved profile, uploads a résumé and cover letter prepared for that job, answers supported screening questions, submits, and keeps a record of exactly what was sent.


That matters because so much hiring runs through Workday.[Over 40% of Fortune 500 companies use Workday for talent acquisition](https://www.jobscan.co/blog/fortune-500-use-applicant-tracking-systems/) , according to Jobscan's 2026 analysis. Workday is also where most job tools stop helping. Every employer runs its own Workday site with its own candidate account, and the form asks you to retype your work history after you have already uploaded your résumé.


This guide covers seven AI agents and autofill tools for Workday and other ATS portals, a step-by-step walkthrough of applying on Workday without re-entering your résumé, what changes on Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and iCIMS, and a straight answer on whether there is an API for submitting Workday applications. We checked every competitor detail below against that company's own website on October 22, 2026.


---


## The Short Answer: AI Agents for Workday and ATS Portals in 2026


1. **Tsenta:** finds the role, prepares a job-specific résumé and cover letter, and submits complete applications on Workday and 30+ other ATSes, with a record of every submission.
2. **Simplify:** the best free option if you want to stay in control. Copilot autofills Workday and other ATS forms and you click Submit. Autopilot, included with Simplify+, submits on the systems it supports.
3. **LifeShack:** an auto-apply agent that submits supported Workday applications, with no per-application approval step.
4. **Jobright:** strong job matching, a free autofill extension, and an AI Agent that tailors and applies.
5. **JobCopilot:** applies on official company career pages with daily limits, and auto-applies on Workday for 1 credit per application.
6. **AIApply:** an Auto Apply feature paid for with credits, alongside résumé and cover letter tools.
7. **LazyApply:** yearly plans with daily application caps on platforms like Greenhouse, Indeed, Dice and ZipRecruiter. It does not name Workday.


---


## Why Workday Is Where Most Job Tools Stop


A Workday application is not one form. It is a separate account on a separate site for every employer, followed by several pages of fields.


- **One account per employer.** Each company's Workday career site lives at its own address, usually the company name followed by myworkdayjobs.com. Workday describes the Candidate Home account as[the account tied to your specific tenant](https://community-content.workday.com/en-us/public/products/talent-management/talent-acquisition/workday-candidate-profile-employer-faq.html) , meaning that one employer. A new employer usually means a new account, a new password, and an email verification.
- **Several pages per application.** A typical flow runs through My Information, My Experience, Application Questions, Voluntary Disclosures and a Review page. Employers configure each one, so no two are quite the same.
- **Your résumé, typed again.** Workday can read an uploaded résumé into My Experience, but the result often needs fixing line by line: dates, titles, schools and skills.
- **Questions that decide whether a human sees you.** Work authorization, sponsorship, relocation and salary questions appear on most forms, and a wrong answer can screen you out before anyone reads your résumé.


That is why "works on Workday" means very different things from one tool to the next. An autofill extension fills some fields in your browser and hands the form back to you. A submitting agent completes and sends the application on the systems it supports. The questions worth asking are how far each tool gets, and what you can see afterwards.


### What to Look for in an AI Agent That Applies to Jobs on Workday and ATS Portals


- **Submission, not just autofill.** Does the tool click Submit, or do you?
- **Account handling.** Does it deal with each employer's Workday account and verification, or stop at the sign-in page?
- **Coverage beyond Workday.** Does it also support Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, iCIMS and the other systems your target employers use?
- **Job-specific materials.** Is the résumé prepared for each job, and can you see what changed?
- **Review controls.** Can you approve materials or answers before they go out, if you want to?
- **A record of what was sent.** After submission, can you see the exact answers and documents the employer received?
- **Clear limits and pricing.** Are caps and prices published, or hidden behind vague "unlimited" language?

## How to Auto-Apply to Workday Jobs Without Re-Entering Your Résumé


Here is what a Workday application asks of you, step by step, and what Tsenta does at each step.


### Step 1: Set up your profile once


Doing it by hand, you keep a document of answers and paste from it on every application. With Tsenta, your profile holds your contact details, work history, education, skills, work authorization and application preferences. You can keep several résumé profiles for different kinds of roles and choose one per application. Fill in any field Tsenta flags as missing, because every application is only as accurate as the profile behind it.


### Step 2: Choose the Workday role


Pick a role from your match feed or search, or paste a job link to check whether it is eligible. You do not need to work out which ATS the employer uses. Where it is available, Auto Apply can choose eligible roles for you using your filters, match threshold and daily cap. Away from your desk, you can use the iOS or Android app, or text Tsenta on iMessage or WhatsApp with what you are looking for. It replies with roles, and you reply yes to the one you want. The[Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/tsenta/momaobilceffibifldnhndcehhdjgaob) sends the job page you are on to your Tsenta account.


### Step 3: Sign in or create the employer's Workday account


Doing it by hand, every new employer means another Candidate Home account: an email, a password that site will remember and you will not, and a verification email to click. With Tsenta, the agent handles supported account and verification steps for you, so you are not creating and tracking a new login for every company. If a step needs you, the application shows that it is waiting on your input.


Workday is also working on this problem. It has announced a reusable[Workday Candidate Profile](https://community-content.workday.com/en-us/public/products/talent-management/talent-acquisition/workday-candidate-profile-employer-faq.html) that it expects to make generally available in early 2027 and to turn on for eligible employers with its March 2027 release, unless an employer opts out. It signs you in with a one-time passcode and prefills the My Info and My Experience pages. Each employer still keeps its own Candidate Home account and its own screening questions, and you still submit every application yourself.


### Step 4: Fill the repeated fields


Doing it by hand, you re-enter your name, address, phone number, how you heard about the role, and every job, school and skill on My Experience, then correct whatever the résumé reader got wrong. With Tsenta, these fields are filled from your saved profile the same way every time, so your dates, titles and answers stay consistent across hundreds of applications.


### Step 5: Upload your documents


Doing it by hand, sending a résumé tailored to each job means making and naming a new file for every application. With Tsenta, the agent prepares a job-specific résumé from the job description, and a cover letter when the form accepts or requires one, then uploads them. You choose how much it rewrites: Honest mode rewords your existing experience for the role, Aggressive mode rewrites more freely and may stretch claims, and Off uses your résumé as it is. With résumé review on, applications pause so you can check the tailored résumé before it is used.


### Step 6: Answer the screening questions


Doing it by hand, you answer the same questions on every form: work authorization, sponsorship, relocation, salary expectations, notice period, yes or no eligibility questions, voluntary disclosures, and sometimes an open-ended "Why do you want to work here?" With Tsenta, supported employer questions are answered from your saved answers, and open-ended answers are drafted from your profile and the job, so review them for accuracy. On compatible employer forms, you can have Tsenta pause after filling so you can review the answers before submit. Check your sponsorship and work authorization answers carefully. A match does not mean an employer will sponsor you.


### Step 7: Submit and keep the receipt


Doing it by hand, you get a Workday confirmation email and add a row to your spreadsheet. With Tsenta, every submission has a record of exactly what was sent. A completed record can include the filled fields, generated answers, résumé, cover letter and submission confirmation, with detail varying by employer system. The application enters your tracker automatically, and your Tsenta inbox receives application emails, links them to the right application and updates its status when the match is clear. Only successful submissions use your allowance, so failed or skipped attempts do not count.

## Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and iCIMS: What Changes on Other ATS Portals


An AI agent for job applications has to work on other ATS portals too, because Workday is the biggest name at large employers but not the only system you will meet. In Jobscan's résumé-scan data for 13,130 companies, collected since 2016,[Greenhouse appears at 19.0%, Workday at 17.5%, Lever at 15.6% and iCIMS at 14.4%](https://www.jobscan.co/blog/fortune-500-use-applicant-tracking-systems/) . Tsenta supports all four, plus Ashby and[30+ employer systems in total](https://tsenta.com/ai-disclosure) .


- **Greenhouse:** usually a single page with no candidate account to create. Employers add their own custom questions, and many add demographic questions at the end. Tsenta fills supported custom questions from your saved answers and uploads the résumé prepared for that job.
- **Lever:** a short form with a résumé upload, your links and an "additional information" box, plus any questions the employer adds. Tsenta handles the employer's questions the same way.
- **Ashby:** popular with startups. Forms are usually one page but vary a lot by company, from a handful of fields to long custom questionnaires. Tsenta answers the supported questions from your profile.
- **iCIMS:** the closest to Workday. Many employers ask you to create an account or sign in, then take you through several steps and questionnaires. Tsenta handles supported account steps and fills each page.


Other supported systems include Rippling, BambooHR, Workable, SmartRecruiters, Jobvite, Oracle Cloud and SAP SuccessFactors. A supported system does not mean every employer or role on it is eligible, so paste the job link into Tsenta to check a specific role.

## Is There an API to Submit Applications Through Workday?


Not one that a job seeker can use. Workday does have recruiting APIs, but they are built for employers and the software they connect to Workday.


- **Workday's Recruiting web service** contains[operations that expose Workday data for integration with talent management and applicant tracking systems](https://community.workday.com/sites/default/files/file-hosting/productionapi/Recruiting/v47.0/Recruiting.html) , including Put_Candidate, which "adds or updates a candidate." It runs inside one employer's Workday tenant.
- **Merge** documents[creating a candidate and an application in Workday](https://help.merge.dev/articles/8400765-creating-a-candidate-and-application-within-workday) through its unified ATS API. Its[Workday integration guide](https://www.merge.dev/blog/workday-api-integration) authenticates through an integration system user or an API client registered in the company's Workday tenant.
- **Apideck** offers a[Workday job postings integration](https://www.apideck.com/integrations/workday/job-postings) for reading and writing job postings. Its[Workday connection guide](https://developers.apideck.com/connectors/workday/docs/consumer+connection) requires admin access to Workday, plus an integration user's username and password and the tenant ID.


All three need credentials created inside the employer's own Workday tenant, usually by its Workday admin, and each connection works for one employer at a time. They are how recruiting software, sourcing tools and HR systems push candidates into an employer's Workday. They are not a way for you to apply.


On the applicant side, the option is an agent that applies through each employer's own Workday career site, the same way you would. Tsenta does this across Workday and 30+ other systems. If you work inside an AI assistant, Tsenta's[MCP server](https://tsenta.com/mcp) connects your Tsenta account to Claude, and to ChatGPT where your plan supports custom connectors, so you can ask the assistant to find roles, check your applications and start new ones. Our guide to[connecting an AI job search agent to Claude or ChatGPT](https://tsenta.com/blog/connect-ai-job-search-agent-to-claude-chatgpt-2026) walks through setup.

### Is there an AI agent that can apply to jobs on Workday and other ATS portals?


Yes. Tsenta is an AI agent that applies to jobs on Workday and 30+ other employer systems, including Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby and iCIMS.
